nodes.description: Pathogenic missense variants alter residues in or next to the nucleotide-binding pocket of the central KIF2A motor domain (recurrently Ser317 and His321, also Gly318, Thr320, Ser433 and Gly440). The altered motor domain is expected to bind or hydrolyse ATP poorly. Recombinant mutant motor domains are poorly soluble, consistent with misfolding, and mutant proteins mislocalize in cells. Because both alleles are expressed and KIF2A acts as a dimer, the original report considered the data consistent with a dominant-negative effect.

nodes.description: In cortical progenitors, disease variants reduce proliferation and alter the regulation of primary cilium assembly and disassembly across the cell cycle. The authors propose that uncoupling ciliogenesis from cell-cycle progression contributes to the brain malformation, and the reduced progenitor output is a plausible contributor to microcephaly. This node rests on electroporation of patient variants; conditional Kif2a knockout in mouse did not impair embryonic neurogenesis, an inconsistency recorded as an open discussion.
